title: Hearing Louis at the Lafayette and becoming Little Jazz
summary: Skeptical of the hype, Roy watched four shows, was floored by Louis's Chinatown, and learned it himself, winning a battle against Chick Webb.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Did he use that even then?

Yeah! He had that for ages. And you know, I actually hadn't heard him in person until the first time I went to hear him... He was at the Lafayette. I think he had Tubby Hall playing drums with him at that time -- that's how I remember it. And Lester Boone, I think, was in the band. Zilner Randolph maybe. Well, anyhow, I went to hear him, because everybody was just talking so much about him, and by this time I really had my feathers up, because I just was mowin' 'em down left and right! -- heh-heh-heh!

So I caught the first show, and I say, "She-ei-i... Is this what they've been shouting about? Get out of here!" And I started to get up and go out, and then I said, ""Wait a minute; this is his first show." And I put myself in his position. Suppose he hung out, and his chops ain't cool, you know. I'd better stay and catch the next show. You know, I figured... I know about that trumpet, man. It can be a devil! It's a bad fella! So I stayed the second show, and it got a little better, you know.
During that time you could sit in the show and get high, you know what I mean. And I lit up, too, because it
was always a sad picture at the Lafayette during those days. So I sit through that, and I got high and sat there until the show come on again.

Now, the third show is when he played this "Chinatown." And see, I always did contend, if you got a rhythm section, you play... A rhythm section that doesn't disturb you but keeps on drivin' you, the shit is gonna sound like it's got to go, you know. And they was chugging on his on this "Chinatown," baby, and man...and it just kept on building. It built, you know. He started down, like, here, and then he went to F up there, he went to A out of there, then he went to C out of there, and right when he got to the C, he was going from the C to the D, and those cats was... They didn't let up one bit! They got just as intense as he did. See, that's what it's supposed to be. Then he hit that note, and everybody stood up, and I looked and I was standing up. I said, "Shit, what's going on?!" I said, "I got to stay for another show."

And I had to catch four shows, and when I seen that last show, I went out and bought the record. You know, what's a funny thing? I hadn't been... I hadn't been... Well, I was getting jobs, but I wasn't as popular as I was after I learned how to play "Chinatown," and ..(?).. made me Little Jazz. That's with Snow's band... Yeah, it was with

Snowden's band, yeah. And we played a battle of music against Chick Webb up at some club on 145th Street, I forget the name of it now, and we played "Chinatown" there, and that wiped everybody out. Because all the vipers was there, you know. And I was in pretty good company from then on, you know.
